# Psalms of Solomon — Psalm 8 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Vindobonensis) | **Section:** Jerusalem's Fall to the Invader

---

**8:1** Trouble and anguish came upon me,
more than upon all the peoples of the earth.

**8:2** Jerusalem heard and was filled with anguish;
her daughters cried aloud for the distress in the land.

**8:3** I clothed myself in sackcloth;
I cried out in prayer to the LORD:

**8:4** 'What have you done against us, O God?
What have we sinned, that you should bring this punishment upon us?'

**8:5** You placed our sins as a burden upon our necks;
you stripped us bare in our affliction.

**8:6** The sons of Israel were scattered throughout the land of strangers;
and there was no one to redeem them.

**8:7** For you drove them out in your anger;

**8:8** because the land was full of lawless deeds and murder and deceit;
and those who committed lawless deeds were without number.

**8:9** The LORD observed all this
and hid his face from them so that no pity would be shown.

**8:10** No man, no woman, no child, not one of their offspring,
escaped from the terrible punishment of the LORD.

**8:11** The sky withheld its rain from them;
the springs of the deep were stopped up before them.

**8:12** For there were no mountains high enough to give them shelter,
nor hills to offer them refuge.

**8:13** Their paths were made more desolate than the ways of the east;
travelers on those paths stumbled as if in darkness.

**8:14** Their sons and their daughters were in grievous captivity,
their neck bearing the seal of slavery.

**8:15** God dealt with them according to their deeds;
he gave them over according to their sins.

**8:16** For God handed them over to all the surrounding nations
to be a reproach and an object of scorn.

**8:17** He had chosen them from among all the nations;
but now he had rejected them in his anger.

**8:18** For their God is their only redeemer —
he is the king of the earth and the righteous judge.

**8:19** For God turned me over, in the intention of my heart, to the man from the east;
and so I bore the yoke of slavery.

**8:20** I watched him advance against Jerusalem with the armies of the nations,
his face filled with dread.

**8:21** He captured the strong towers and the walls of Jerusalem;
and God permitted it.

**8:22** The ruler of the nations came up to Jerusalem
and set his foot upon her neck;

**8:23** and he did not spare her beautiful young men;
he put the young men to the sword.

**8:24** He drove away the leaders of Jerusalem beyond the borders of the land
and sent their young men to the distant sea.

**8:25** He made the daughter of Jerusalem a laughingstock among the nations;
her sons and daughters were in miserable captivity.

**8:26** Because the sons of Israel had defiled the holy things of the LORD
and had profaned with their lawless deeds the offerings of God.

**8:27** He set God's altar before them as a stone for treading upon;
all their glory he turned to shame.

**8:28** He revealed the sins of Jerusalem before the nations;
her beauty was laid out as spoil before every nation under heaven.

**8:29** He spread her sins before the sun in open shame;
and all the earth witnessed the righteous judgment of God.

**8:30** Hidden away are the judgments of God in the farthest parts of the earth;
who can comprehend the justice of God except the one who fears him in knowledge?

**8:31** One who understands these things will vindicate the LORD in his judgments;
for he is righteous, and those who do not understand will say nothing.

**8:32** For the mercy of the LORD is upon those who fear him,
through which he distinguishes in judgment between the righteous and the sinner.

**8:33** Blessed is the LORD who judges the earth in his righteousness.

**8:34** Israel, give praise to the LORD by the mercy of God;
and let us bless the name of the LORD forever and ever.

---

*LOGOS notes: Formal English rendering following Greek syntax. Poetic lineation preserved.*
